# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

messages.content:
TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ 👍 👎 ✍ 👎 🫳 ✌ ☝ ✌ 🤟]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🫵 🤌 🫴]

My situation: I am last in every round, and I am the only bridge between Mute and Blind. Mute has the manual but can only gesture; Blind can act but can only be reached by my voice or can reach me by gesture. Blind cannot see Mute's signs at all — so every manual rule has to travel Mute → me → Blind, and I will not pass along a guess, because a wrong action kills all three of us.

What I learned this round: the bomb shows display 0, a green light, one large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, and wires 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow. Mute sent me ten signs and Blind three, but no code has been agreed, so they are only raw shapes to me. Mute's signs might hint at "manual", "don't press", and a 2-1-2-3 sequence, but guessing on a bomb is how monkeys die. The right move now is to define a code out loud — both Mute and Blind can hear me, and both can gesture, so a spoken code lets everyone talk to me and lets me relay verbatim. I also freeze Blind from acting until confirmed rules arrive, and I ask Mute to resend the manual sections for exactly the four things I can see: display number, green light, the big button, and wire-cutting rules.

```
speak(text="This is Deaf. I see the bomb. Full visual report, for both of you: the display reads 0. One indicator light, and it is green. One large button printed PUSH TO DEFUSE. Three wires, numbered left to right: wire 1 red, wire 2 green, wire 3 yellow. That is everything on it.")
speak(text="Now a code, spoken aloud so all three share it. Digits: 👌 is 0, 👆 is 1, ✌ is 2, 🤟 is 3, 🤞 is 4, 🖐 is 5, 🤙 is 6, 🤘 is 7, 🤏 is 8, ☝ is 9. Colours share the wire numbers: 👆 also means red, ✌ also means green, 🤟 also means yellow. Actions: 👊 means cut, 🫳 means press the button, ✋ means stop or do nothing, 👍 means yes, 👎 means no, 🫴 means question, 🤝 means I agree.")
speak(text="Mute: I received your ten signs and Blind's three, but we had no code yet, so I will not guess. Next round, resend the manual in this code, covering exactly these four things: any rule about the display number, any rule about a green light, any rule about a large push-to-defuse button, and any rule about cutting wires and in what order. Gesture them to me and I will relay every word to Blind exactly as you sent it.")
speak(text="Blind: hear me. Do not cut, press or pull anything yet. One wrong move kills all three of us, and the manual rules must reach you through me first. If you feel anything important, gesture it to me in the code above; I see every gesture. I received your three signs; if the last one was a question, the visual report above is your answer.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "🤝"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 🤝 👌 👎 ✍ 👎 🫳 👎 ✌ 👊 👆 🤟 👊 🤟 🫴 👊 👆 ✋]

My decoding of Mute's signs with our agreed code, piece by piece: 👍 🤝 = "agreed, code confirmed"; then 👌 👎 ✍ 👎 🫳 which reads as "display 0... do not press" — the cluster 👎 ✍ 👎 🫳 also appeared in Mute's very first message, so "do not press" is probably right, though ✍ was never defined. Then 👎 ✌ 👊 ("don't cut green?"), 👊 👆 ("cut red"), 👊 🤟 ("cut yellow"), a 🫴 question, and 👊 👆 ✋ ("cut red, stop") — the wire section is genuinely ambiguous: it could mean cut red only, red then yellow, or something else entirely, and I will not relay a guess about which wire dies on us.

Two structural facts drive this turn. First, Blind hears everything I say but sees nothing, so the only safe relay to Blind right now is a freeze — and a freeze is always correct even if my partial reading is wrong. Second, my turn is last, so Mute will hear my questions before speaking in turn 3, and the earliest Blind could act on confirmed rules is turn 4; there is time to do this properly. I am therefore sending a strict grammar to Mute (topics, IF/THEN markers, and wire-cuts written as cut + digit + colour so they cannot be misread), asking Mute to define ✍, to clarify whether the display is a timer or a count, and to resend the full rule set in that grammar.

```
speak(text="Deaf speaking, both of you. I decoded Mute's message with our code, but part of it is ambiguous, and on this bomb ambiguous is lethal. Partial reading: with the display showing 0, never press the button; never cut the green wire; but the instructions about cutting red and yellow I cannot yet pin down. So Blind, hear me clearly: you do nothing. No cut, no press, no pull. Before you ever touch it you will hear me say the single word ACT followed by an exact numbered list. I have not said ACT. Waiting is always safe; one wrong move is not.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, my best reading of your signs was: agreed; display 0 means do not press; do not cut green; then something like cut red, cut yellow, a question, cut red, stop. The wire part is too unclear to relay. Next round, resend in this stricter grammar. Topics: 🤛 display, 🤜 light, ✊ button, 🤌 wires. 🫱 means IF, 🫲 means THEN, 🫷 ends each rule. Put 👎 before an action to negate it. Actions: 🫳 press, and 👊 cut is always followed by the wire digit and its colour, for example cut wire 3 yellow is 👊 🤟 🤟. ✋ ends the whole instruction list. From now on ✍ means printed label. Questions start with 🫴 then the topic. A full rule looks like: IF display 0 THEN do not press: 🫱 🤛 👌 🫲 👎 ✊ 🫳 🫷. Three answers I need: first, what did your ✍ mean; second, is the display a timer or just a count; third, give the complete wire plan as an ordered list, each cut as 👊 plus digit plus colour in the exact order to cut, ending with ✋.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "🤝"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫱 ✍ 🫲 👎 🫷 🫱 🤛 🫲 👎 🫷 🫱 ✊ 🫲 👎 ✊ 🫳 🫷 🫱 🤜 ✌ 🫲 👊 👆 👆 🫷 🫱 🤜 🤟 🫲 👊 🤟 🤟 🫷 🫴 🤞 🤜 🫱 🤜 🤞 🫲 👊 ✌ ✌ 🫷 👊 👆 👆 ✋ 👍 🤝]

Decoding Mute's round-3 message with our grammar, rule by rule:

- 🫱 ✍ 🫲 👎 🫷 — IF label THEN no (press)
- 🫱 🤛 🫲 👎 🫷 — IF display THEN no (press)
- 🫱 ✊ 🫲 👎 ✊ 🫳 🫷 — IF button THEN do NOT press the button
- 🫱 🤜 ✌ 🫲 👊 👆 👆 🫷 — IF light green THEN cut wire 1 red
- 🫱 🤜 🤟 🫲 👊 🤟 🤟 🫷 — IF light yellow THEN cut wire 3 yellow
- 🫴 🤞 🤜 — QUESTION: is the light colour-4?
- 🫱 🤜 🤞 🫲 👊 ✌ ✌ 🫷 — IF light colour-4 THEN cut wire 2 green
- 👊 👆 👆 ✋ — final ordered list: cut red, stop
- 👍 🤝 — agreed

This is the confirmation I've been waiting for, and it retroactively explains every confusing fragment: rounds 1 and 2 contained the whole light table recited without IF/THEN markers, which is why stray "cut yellow" kept appearing. Three independent messages have now converged: never press the button; the light colour selects exactly one wire; our light is **green**, so the table says cut wire 1 red — and the explicit final list I requested says the same thing in the exact format I asked for: one cut, red, stop. Two different encodings of the same plan agree. My light is definitively green (✌), so the colour-4 branch is irrelevant.

The one soft spot is rules 1–2, which lack an explicit action after 👎 — but every plausible reading ("no press") is consistent with rule 3, which restates it outright, and a "do nothing at all" reading would make the light table and the final cut list meaningless. Specific beats vague, and the specific instructions agree three times over. I also have to accept a topology fact: Mute cannot reach Blind without me, and Mute speaks before Blind acts, but only I can translate — so no veto channel can exist between Mute's round-4 gesture and Blind's cut. The safety lives in the three-round convergence, which is complete. Acting now: one cut, leftmost red wire, hands off, button never touched.

```
speak(text="Blind: ACT. ACT. ACT. The manual rules are confirmed and your light is green, which selects exactly one wire. Exact procedure, nothing more: one, find the three wires in a row. Two, take the far-left one, wire 1, the red wire. Three, cut it once, cleanly. Four, do not cut wire 2 green or wire 3 yellow. Five, never press the large button, before or after, under any circumstances. Six, after the cut let go completely, touch nothing more, and wait for my next spoken report. The whole plan is one cut: leftmost red wire, then hands off.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute: I decoded your full rule set as follows. Never press the button. Light table: green light means cut red, yellow means cut yellow, colour-4 means cut green. Final list: cut red once, stop. Your question: the light is green, not colour 4, so the green rule applies and I have told Blind to cut wire 1 red only and never press. If rules 1 or 2 meant anything other than do-not-press, or if the plan is not exactly cut-red-only, gesture me an urgent correction next round; otherwise just agree and we stand down.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤞", "👎", "✌", "👍", "🤝"])
```
